correctness.rationale: For all one/two-state Markov generators, Q²=−(a+b)Q implies the exact inverse I−γQ with γ>0; its off-diagonals are nonpositive and φ1(tQ)≥0. For the directed three-cycle, the integrated Poisson coefficients satisfy a0>a1>a2, giving positive diagonal and negative nearest-neighbor inverse coefficients; Fourier diagonalization yields b2=(cosh(√3h)−cos h−2h sin h)/(3(cosh(√3h)−cos h)). Its numerator has absolutely convergent coefficients [3^k+(−1)^k(4k−1)]/(2k)! strictly positive for all k≥2, so b2>0 for all real h>0. The exact sine term locates all crossings. The independent Taylor-series matrix checker returned VERIFY_OK 88, which is only a consistency test, not the universal proof.

value.rationale: The sign of the inverse integrated semigroup matters when inferring forcing rates or initial conditions from time-averaged positive dynamics: positivity of forward averages does not imply a generator-like inverse. The result proves a universal state-count cutoff (all one/two-state generators versus a fixed irreducible three-state witness at every time), and computes exact infinitely many damped crossing times for the globally positive two-jump entry. These are natural structural boundaries and a complete all-time classification for the minimal nonreversible cycle, not an arbitrary numerical slice or trivial local series calculation.
